name: Critical materials and geopolitics
thesis: China's export controls on rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony and graphite turned critical materials from a commodity trade into a national security trade, and the US government responded by becoming an equity owner, offtaker and price floor provider (MP Materials, Lithium Americas, Trilogy Metals, Vulcan Elements, Korea Zinc, Intel). Policy now underwrites the downside for selected Western producers, which changes the risk profile for long term holders and makes these names more attractive for put selling than their volatile history suggests. The near term swing factor is the expiry of China's one year suspensions in November 2026 (rare earth rules on November 10, gallium, germanium and antimony ban on November 27). Copper is the large cap anchor: grid and data center demand plus the Grasberg disruption pushed prices to records in 2026.

facts: July 2025: US Department of Defense agreed a $110/kg NdPr oxide price floor for 10 years and a 10 year offtake for 100% of the 10X magnet facility output.
DoD invested $400 million in MP preferred equity plus warrants, about 15% of shares on a fully converted basis, making it the largest shareholder (July 2025).
10X facility targets 10,000 metric tons of annual magnet capacity by 2028 with a $140 million annual EBITDA guarantee with 2% escalator; JPMorgan and Goldman committed $1.0 billion of financing.
DoD also committed a $150 million loan to expand heavy rare earth separation at Mountain Pass.

pipeline.product: Expiry of China's one year suspension of October 2025 rare earth export rules
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Three paths: extension, selective reinstatement, or full reimposition. April 2025 case by case licensing for seven medium and heavy rare earths (including dysprosium) stays in force regardless. Reimposition would spike non China heavy rare earth prices and benefit MP, Lynas, Energy Fuels and USA Rare Earth.

pipeline.product: Expiry of China's suspension of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials export ban to the US
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Military end user ban remains in effect regardless. Reinstatement would favor Alcoa (gallium), Umicore and Teck (germanium), Perpetua and US Antimony.

pipeline.product: Project Vault strategic stockpile ($10 billion EXIM loan plus $1.67 billion private)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Creates a committed buyer for antimony, cobalt, copper, graphite, nickel and others; aims for 60 days of emergency supply. Supports price floors for Western producers.

pipeline.product: Alcoa Wagerup gallium project (US, Australia, Japan)
pipeline.timing: Final investment decision July 14, 2026; groundbreaking late August 2026
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: About 100 tonnes per year of gallium, roughly 10% of global supply, with $174 million Pentagon financing. First meaningful non China gallium source.

pipeline.timing: Blocks 2 and 3 restarted from Q2 2026. The mill ran at about 67% of normal (about 140,000 tonnes of ore a day) in Q3 2026, short of the earlier 85% goal for H2 2026; Freeport now aims for 80% by mid 2027 and near full output by the end of 2027 (Northern Miner, Oct 2, 2026). Block 1 in 2027.
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Restores copper supply; Freeport guides about 1.6 billion lb per year average for 2027 to 2029 from PTFI. A smooth ramp caps copper upside; delays extend the deficit.

pipeline.product: Energy Fuels heavy rare earth Phase 1B
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: About 20 tonnes terbium oxide and 120 tonnes dysprosium oxide per year, a rare non China heavy rare earth source.
$7.4 billion US smelter with the US Department of War holding 40% of the JV; adds US refining of zinc, lead and byproduct critical metals.

layers.name: Copper mining and smelting
layers.why: Copper is the wiring of electrification, data centers and defense, and new mine supply is slow while existing mines face disruptions.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Grasberg force majeure removed about 525,000 tonnes across 2025 and 2026 per Goldman Sachs; Section 232 tariffs split US and global prices. COMEX hit a record $6.82/lb on August 6, 2026.

companies.name: Freeport-McMoRan
companies.role: Largest US listed copper miner; Grasberg and US mines
companies.note: Grasberg ramp is the key 2026 to 2027 variable. The mill ran at about 67% of normal in Q3 2026, behind the earlier 85% goal; target is 80% by mid 2027.

companies.name: Southern Copper
companies.role: Large copper reserves in Peru and Mexico
companies.note: Majority owned by Grupo Mexico.

companies.name: Teck Resources
companies.role: Copper miner; Trail smelter produces germanium
companies.note: Merger with Anglo American announced 2025 (status unverified).

companies.name: BHP Group
companies.role: Largest diversified miner, Escondida copper
companies.note: Iron ore still the biggest earner.

companies.name: Rio Tinto
companies.role: Copper (Oyu Tolgoi, Kennecott) and lithium (Arcadium)
companies.note: Kennecott is one of two US primary copper smelters.

companies.name: Ivanhoe Mines
companies.role: Kamoa-Kakula copper in DRC
companies.note: US OTC IVPAF.

companies.name: Hudbay Minerals
companies.role: Copper producer, Copper World project in Arizona
companies.note: US domestic copper development.

companies.name: Taseko Mines
companies.role: Gibraltar mine and Florence copper in Arizona
companies.note: Small US in situ copper producer.

companies.name: Trilogy Metals
companies.role: Upper Kobuk copper and zinc projects in Alaska Ambler district
companies.note: US government closed a $35.6 million investment for about 10% plus warrants tied to Ambler Road.

companies.name: Korea Zinc
companies.role: Largest zinc and lead smelter; building $7.4 billion Tennessee smelter
companies.note: US Department of War to hold 40% of the US JV; US partners get about 10% of Korea Zinc via $1.9 billion new shares.

layers.name: Rare earth mining and separation
layers.why: China dominates separation, especially of heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) that magnets need for heat resistance.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Heavy rare earth separation outside China is near zero; Lynas paused its Texas plant plans and focuses on Malaysia; April 2025 Chinese licensing on seven heavy elements remains in force.

companies.name: MP Materials
companies.role: Mountain Pass mine, separation, and magnet making (Independence and 10X)
companies.note: DoD price floor $110/kg NdPr, offtake, and about 15% stake.

companies.name: Lynas Rare Earths
companies.role: Largest non China separated rare earth producer (Australia, Malaysia)
companies.note: US OTC LYSCF. H1 FY2026 revenue A$413.7 million, net profit A$80.2 million; JARE contracts include $110/kg NdPr floor.

companies.name: Energy Fuels
companies.role: Monazite processing and heavy rare earth separation at White Mesa, Utah; uranium
companies.note: $104 million Phase 1B targets 20 t Tb and 120 t Dy oxide by Q4 2027.

companies.name: Iluka Resources
companies.role: Mineral sands and Eneabba rare earth refinery (Australian government funded)
companies.note: US OTC ILKAF.

companies.name: Neo Performance Materials
companies.role: Rare earth processing and magnet plant in Estonia
companies.note: Thin US OTC; acquisition status unverified.

layers.name: Permanent magnets
layers.why: Magnets go into EV motors, wind turbines, drones, missiles and robots; magnet making is where China's hold is tightest.
layers.bottleneck_reason: US capacity is small and new; MP 10X (2028), Vulcan Elements (10,000 tonne target) and Noveon are years from scale.

companies.name: USA Rare Earth
companies.role: Stillwater, Oklahoma magnet plant and Round Top deposit
companies.note: Commerce Department equity stake reported (terms unverified). Pre revenue.

companies.name: Vulcan Elements
companies.role: US rare earth magnet maker
companies.note: $1.4 billion package with ReElement: $620 million DoD loan, $50 million Commerce equity, $550 million private. Private company.

companies.name: Noveon Magnetics
companies.role: Texas sintered magnet maker using recycled feed
companies.note: Signed memorandum with Lynas for a US magnet supply chain. Private.

layers.name: Gallium, germanium, antimony and tungsten
layers.why: These small volume metals are essential for chips, radar, night vision, munitions and armor, and China controls most refined supply.
layers.bottleneck_reason: China export ban to the US is suspended only until November 27, 2026 and the military end user ban remains; tungsten reference prices went from about $485/MTU in August 2025 to about $1,775/MTU by February 2026.

companies.name: Alcoa
companies.role: Gallium recovery at Wagerup alumina refinery
companies.note: About 100 t/yr gallium project, FID July 2026, $174 million Pentagon support. Mostly an aluminum company.

companies.name: Umicore
companies.role: Germanium refining and recycling
companies.note: US OTC UMICY.

companies.name: Perpetua Resources
companies.role: Stibnite gold and antimony project in Idaho
companies.note: Most prominent potential US primary antimony source; development stage.

companies.name: United States Antimony
companies.role: Only US antimony smelter (Montana)
companies.note: Small cap with DLA supply contracts (amounts unverified).

companies.name: Almonty Industries
companies.role: Tungsten miner: Panasqueira (Portugal), Sangdong (Korea)
companies.note: Nasdaq ticker ALM (verify). US restrictions on Chinese tungsten for defense from 2027 support pricing.

layers.name: Lithium and battery materials
layers.why: Lithium demand is now driven by grid storage as well as EVs, and the 2024 to 2025 glut is unwinding.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Supply is ample globally, but CATL's Jianxiawo mine suspension and capex cuts tightened the market; battery grade carbonate was about $24,000 to $25,000/t in May 2026, up about 60% year to date.

companies.name: Albemarle
companies.role: Largest Western lithium producer
companies.note: Only US lithium producer at scale (Silver Peak). Highly cyclical.

companies.name: Sociedad Quimica y Minera
companies.role: Chilean lithium brine producer
companies.note: Codelco partnership.

companies.name: Lithium Americas
companies.role: Thacker Pass, Nevada lithium project with GM
companies.note: DOE took 5% of LAC plus 5% of the Thacker Pass JV tied to the $2.26 billion loan.

companies.name: Standard Lithium
companies.role: Arkansas brine direct lithium extraction with Equinor
companies.note: Development stage.

companies.name: Syrah Resources
companies.role: Graphite mine (Mozambique) and Vidalia, Louisiana anode plant
companies.note: Graphite is on China's control list; thin US OTC.

layers.name: Uranium and nuclear fuel
layers.why: Uranium is now on the US critical minerals list and Russian enriched uranium is being phased out, while reactor demand rises.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Enrichment and conversion are concentrated; Centrus is the only US HALEU producer.

companies.name: Cameco
companies.role: Uranium mining, conversion, Westinghouse stake
companies.note: Q2 2026 realized uranium price about $78.50/lb. Spot price reports in our searches conflicted ($89.63 vs above $120), so treat spot as unverified.

companies.name: Centrus Energy
companies.role: US enrichment and HALEU
companies.note: $900 million DOE HALEU task order.

companies.name: Uranium Energy Corp
companies.role: US uranium producer
companies.note: Beta to uranium sentiment.

layers.name: Industrial gases and helium
layers.why: Helium is essential for chip fabs, MRI and aerospace, and about a third of world supply comes from Qatar LNG.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Qatar's LNG halt during the 2026 Iran conflict cut roughly one third of global helium supply; early spot price increases of about 50% were reported in March 2026.

companies.name: Linde
companies.role: Largest industrial gas company, helium distribution and storage
companies.note: Merchant gas layer controls allocation of scarce helium.

companies.name: Air Products
companies.role: Industrial gases with large helium position
companies.note: Analysts cited helium pricing as a 2026 tailwind.

companies.name: Air Liquide
companies.role: Industrial gases including helium
companies.note: US OTC AIQUY.

layers.name: Downstream users and US government backed manufacturing
layers.why: End users like chipmakers and defense primes are the customers that policy is trying to secure, and some now have the government as a shareholder.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Users can pay up for materials, but a cutoff halts production lines (2025 rare earth license delays briefly stopped some auto lines).

companies.name: Intel
companies.role: US chipmaker; government holds about 9.9%
companies.note: 433.3 million shares at $20.47 ($8.9 billion), August 2025.

companies.name: General Motors
companies.role: Thacker Pass partner, Project Vault participant, magnet offtaker
companies.note: User side; hurt by shortages.

companies.name: L3Harris
companies.role: Aerojet solid rocket motors; DoD $1 billion convertible preferred in Missile Solutions unit (April 2026)
companies.note: Overlaps with defense theme; heavy user of critical minerals.

second_order.idea: Government equity stakes as a de facto put under strategic names
second_order.why: Price floors, offtakes and federal ownership limit downside fundamentals, which can make cash secured puts on pullbacks attractive. Volatility stays high because headlines drive prices.

second_order.idea: Recyclers and processors of scrap and e-waste
second_order.why: Recycling is the fastest non China source of germanium, rare earths and cobalt.

second_order.idea: Industrial gas majors as helium toll collectors
second_order.why: Helium disruption raises merchant pricing while the core gas business stays steady, a low volatility way to own scarcity.

second_order.idea: Defense users facing input cost and supply risk
second_order.why: From 2027 US defense procurement restricts Chinese tungsten; magnet and gallium shortages could delay munitions and radar.

second_order.idea: Copper users squeezed by tariffs and record prices
second_order.why: HVAC and wire makers face higher costs under the 2026 country by country Section 232 copper tariffs (impact unverified per company).

risks.risk: China extends suspensions or eases controls, collapsing scarcity premiums
risks.signal: MOFCOM announcements before November 10 and November 27, 2026.

risks.risk: China dumps rare earths or gallium to undercut new Western supply
risks.signal: Chinese NdPr and gallium export prices falling while volumes rise.

risks.risk: Policy reversal or political change ending floors and stakes
risks.signal: Congressional appropriations, court challenges to federal equity deals, 2026 midterm results.

risks.risk: Copper demand disappointment or Grasberg faster restart
risks.signal: LME and COMEX inventory builds; narrowing COMEX vs LME premium; Chinese copper imports.

risks.risk: Development stage execution risk (permits, cost overruns, dilution)
risks.signal: Equity raises, construction delays, capex revisions.

risks.risk: Lithium price rebound reverses as Chinese lepidolite restarts
risks.signal: Restart of CATL Jianxiawo mine; Chinese carbonate futures.

indicators.name: China MOFCOM export control notices
indicators.cadence: Event driven, watch weekly into November

indicators.name: NdPr oxide price (China and ex China)
indicators.why: Compare to $110/kg DoD floor; early August 2026 NdPr alloy was about $133.67/kg

indicators.name: COMEX vs LME copper price spread
indicators.why: Measures tariff driven US premium; COMEX record $6.82/lb on Aug 6, 2026; about $6.66/lb on Oct 9, 2026 (Trading Economics)

indicators.name: US federal deal announcements (DoD Office of Strategic Capital, DOE LPO, Commerce, EXIM)
indicators.why: New equity stakes or floors re-rate targets quickly

indicators.name: Grasberg production updates
indicators.why: Largest swing factor for copper supply

indicators.name: Helium spot and contract pricing
indicators.why: Recovery of Qatar supply ends the price spike

changes.what: Freeport's Grasberg mill ran at about 67% of normal in Q3 2026, short of the earlier 85% goal, and the new target is 80% by mid 2027. Copper supply stays tighter for longer, with COMEX copper about $6.66/lb on Oct 9.
